beads.title: Answer a disco ping that arrives over DERP, so a Go peer's tailscale ping gets its pong
beads.description: A disco ping that reaches this node over DERP is thrown away, so a Go peer running `tailscale ping` against this node while the two are on DERP never gets a pong. At commit e2ed432399c9b0fda7aa14e9eb27784d2d893c55 a Go client's endpoint.discoPing (wgengine/magicsock/endpoint.go line 1038) sends a pingCLI disco ping to the peer's DERP address whenever it has one (lines 1058 to 1059), as well as to any UDP candidates. The Go node that receives it answers over DERP. processDERPReadResult (wgengine/magicsock/derp.go line 734) passes a DERP-borne disco frame to handleDiscoMessage with srcAddr set to 127.3.3.40:<regionID> (tailcfg.DerpMagicIPAddr) and derpNodeSrc set to the frame's source node key (line 751). handlePingLocked (wgengine/magicsock/magicsock.go line 2512) then refuses a Geneve-encapsulated ping over DERP (lines 2518 to 2522), counts the node only if that source node key is a known peer (lines 2564 to 2567), logs and sends nothing when it is not (lines 2590 to 2593), and otherwise sends Pong{TxID, Src: src.ap} back to derpNodeSrc on that DERP address (lines 2603 to 2608). This repository drops the ping. ts_runtime::multiderp's demux_relayed_disco (ts_runtime/src/multiderp.rs line 631) hands DERP-borne disco to MagicSock::handle_relayed_disco (ts_magicsock/src/sock.rs line 1385). That handler acts on CallMeMaybe and CallMeMaybeVia only and discards every other message (line 1411), and the test relayed_ping_is_dropped (sock.rs line 5274) pins the drop. The reason given in both places is that a DERP frame has no UDP source to answer. That reason is about host-sourced sends and does not apply here: Go's pong goes to a node key over the DERP connection, never to an address. The effect is visible to peers: `tailscale ping` from a Go peer prints no 'pong from ... via DERP(region)' line and times out, while the node is working. The pieces exist. The region runner that calls demux_relayed_disco already holds the source node key (peer_id, multiderp.rs line 552) and its own region id, and disco::seal_pong builds the pong. Decision to make, and to record: this tree's direct-path ping admission (MagicSock::handle_disco) is stricter than Go's, because it requires the ping's claimed node key to be bound to the sender's disco key. Keep that rule on the DERP arm or not, and if kept, check the binding against the DERP source node key, which is the key Go's unambiguousNodeKeyOfPingLocked (magicsock.go line 2478) trusts first. Port the refusals with the reply, and test them through the production demux rather than by rebuilding the expected frame. A ping from a node key that is not a current peer gets no pong. A Geneve-framed ping over DERP gets no pong. The pong goes to the source node key, on the region the ping arrived on, with its Src field set to 127.3.3.40:<that region>. No candidate path is learned from a DERP-borne ping; relayed_ping_is_dropped already asserts that and must keep asserting it once it stops asserting the drop. See PORTING.md section B.

beads.title: Bind a peer-relay handshake to the address that challenged it, as Go's relayManager does
beads.description: The peer-relay handshake here accepts relayed pings and pongs from any address on the endpoint's VNI. Go binds the handshake to the one address whose challenge it answered. At commit e2ed432399c9b0fda7aa14e9eb27784d2d893c55, relayManager.handleRxDiscoMsgRunLoop (wgengine/magicsock/relaymanager.go line 584) records addrPortVNI{event.from, event.vni} for a handshake when it accepts that handshake's BindUDPRelayEndpointChallenge (lines 611 to 635). A relayed Pong is passed to the handshake only if its own source and VNI equal that key, and is otherwise discarded as 'No outstanding work tied to this [addrPortVNI]' (lines 658 to 663). A relayed Ping is always ponged at its source (line 648), but it reaches the handshake, and so triggers a ping back, only under the same key (lines 653 to 657). The handshake loop also ignores a relayed ping until its answer has been sent (lines 983 to 986). The path that becomes usable is done.pongReceivedFrom (line 735), which is the challenge's source by construction. This repository binds nothing to that address. RelayPath records it as answered_addr (ts_magicsock/src/relay.rs line 154) and uses it only to aim retry pings. MagicSock::handle_relay_ping (ts_magicsock/src/sock.rs line 1693) checks only that the sender has a relay path on this VNI, then pings back at the relayed ping's own source (line 1743) in any handshake state. A ping from an address that never challenged this node therefore puts an in-flight ping at that address, and the pong to it confirms a path there, because RelayPath::note_pong (relay.rs line 205) confirms whatever address the matching ping was sent to. MagicSock::handle_relay_pong (sock.rs line 1761) matches on transaction id alone, then writes the pong's own source into the inbound attribution map beside the confirmed address (line 1823). #458 made that pong branch source-agnostic on the ground that upstream takes the source as given. That is true of upstream's refresh pongs once a path is in use, which endpoint.handlePongConnLocked (wgengine/magicsock/endpoint.go line 1917) matches by transaction id. It is not true of the handshake's pong, and #458's test a_relayed_pong_from_any_source_still_confirms_the_path pins a handshake pong from an address that did not challenge. The port: while the handshake is unconfirmed, key both the ping back and pong acceptance on (answered_addr, VNI). Keep ponging a relayed ping at its source whether or not the key matches, still behind relay_reply_target_allowed, which is a recorded fork restriction and stays. Keep refresh pongs after confirmation matched by transaction id, as Go does. Decide whether a pong's differing source still belongs in the attribution map, and write the reason at set_confirmed_addrs. Test through handle_relay_disco, not by rebuilding the state. During the handshake, a pong with a valid transaction id from an address other than the challenger must not confirm the path. A relayed ping from such an address must be ponged, but must put no ping on the wire toward it. A relayed ping before any challenge was answered must trigger no ping back. The existing a_relay_message_from_a_forbidden_source_is_dropped must keep passing. Re-pin #458's test to upstream's rule rather than deleting it. A real relay server answers from the address that challenged, so a Go peer sees no difference. What differs is which inputs this node's handshake state machine acts on. See PORTING.md section B.

beads.title: Port Go's CallMeMaybe admission refusals: DERP only, bound to the DERP sender, Via only from relay-capable peers
beads.description: A CallMeMaybe or CallMeMaybeVia is acted on here after one check, that the sealing disco key belongs to some netmap member. Go refuses three more cases first. At commit e2ed432399c9b0fda7aa14e9eb27784d2d893c55, handleDiscoMessage's CallMeMaybe arm (wgengine/magicsock/magicsock.go lines 2298 to 2385) applies them in order. (1) Arrival path. The message must have arrived over DERP with a non-zero source node key, else it is dropped as '[unexpected] %s packets should only come via DERP' (lines 2312 to 2316). The UDP receive path passes a zero derpNodeSrc (line 1827), so Go never acts on a CallMeMaybe that arrives on the UDP socket. (2) Sender binding. The DERP source node key must be a known peer (lines 2317 to 2327), and the disco key that sealed the message must be one of that peer's disco keys, per endpoint.checkAndUpdateDiscoKey (wgengine/magicsock/endpoint.go line 1637). Otherwise the message is dropped as 'from peer via DERP whose netmap discokey != disco source' (lines 2346 to 2358) and counted in metricRecvDiscoCallMeMaybeBadDisco or metricRecvDiscoCallMeMaybeViaBadDisco. (3) CallMeMaybeVia only. The sending peer must be relay-capable, i.e. endpoint.relayCapable = capVerIsRelayCapable(n.Cap()) (endpoint.go line 1747), else 'is not known to be relay capable' (lines 2341 to 2344). This repository carries none of the three. MagicSock::handle_disco (ts_magicsock/src/sock.rs line 2420) acts on a CallMeMaybe received directly on the UDP socket, learning its endpoints and pinging them at once, where Go drops it. MagicSock::handle_relayed_disco (sock.rs line 1385) receives only the frame, because demux_relayed_disco (ts_runtime/src/multiderp.rs line 631) drops the source node key its caller holds (peer_id, line 552). So call_me_maybe_sender_allowed (sock.rs line 2072) can ask only whether the sealing disco key belongs to some member, not whether it belongs to the node whose DERP connection delivered it. And CapabilityVersion::is_relay_capable (ts_capabilityversion/src/lib.rs line 402) is ported, its doc comment names the inbound CallMeMaybeVia gate as one of the two things it gates in Go, and nothing outside that crate's own tests calls it. A Go peer sends both messages only over DERP, from its own node key, and sends CallMeMaybeVia only to relay-capable peers, so a Go peer sees no difference. What differs is which inputs this node acts on, and each difference is an upstream refusal that was not ported. The port, in four parts. Carry the DERP source node key to handle_relayed_disco. Drop CallMeMaybe on the UDP arm. Bind the sealing disco key to the DERP sender; the binding verifier already answers that exact question when it is given a node key. Gate CallMeMaybeVia on the sending peer's capability version, which needs the peer's Node.Cap to reach magicsock. Read this with the disable-relay-client entry: it adds a fourth refusal to the same Via arm (magicsock.go line 2331), and if both are taken together they should share the change. Test through the production entry points. A CallMeMaybe on the UDP socket learns no endpoint and sends no ping. A DERP-borne CallMeMaybe sealed by peer A's disco key but delivered from peer B's node key learns nothing, and the same frame from A's node key still works. A CallMeMaybeVia from a peer at capability version 120 starts no bind handshake, while one from a peer at 121 does. See PORTING.md section B.
